osaka_sushi_hamuro.gf_detail: Not gluten-free in practice: soy sauce and simmered dishes throughout an omakase.
osaka_sushi_hamuro.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a sushi and seafood counter.
osaka_sushi_hamuro.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 17:00–23:00 (L.O. 22:30); closed Sundays, open holidays, plus irregular days (Tabelog). Hard to reserve (January 2026). Cards accepted (Tabelog).
osaka_sushi_hamuro.notes: [Sushi · a six-seat alley counter off Shinsaibashi-suji] A six-seat sushi counter at the end of a narrow alley, where only the sign shows from the street. It's been open since 2015, and the owner has thirty years of experience. The meal is an omakase of seasonal fish, sushi and small dishes, and you can add favorites. Diners remember the kohada (one called it the best ever), sweet red sea urchin, nodoguro, katsuo tataki, crab, and winter fugu milt. It finishes with ushiojiru. The chef pairs sake to the food. The owner is gentle and the room calm, and regulars keep it full; reservations are hard to get. Courses are good value, drinks less so. Reviewers spent about ¥10,000–30,000.

chef_bio.background: Owner with 30 years of experience (April 2024 review).

anecdotes.text: "The crab, nodoguro (blackthroat sea perch), and katsuo (skipjack tuna) tataki were incredible… The kohada (gizzard shad) was the best I've ever had." — September 2024.
"The owner has a gentle demeanor, making it a comfortable place to enjoy a leisurely meal. I ordered the omakase and added a few of my favorite dishes." — December 2025.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ(店舗会員): 鮓 羽室、大阪市中央区心斎橋筋2-6-19、心斎橋駅4B出口・なんば駅14番出口から徒歩5分、月〜土17:00〜23:00(L.O.22:30)、日曜休み(祝日は営業)、不定休あり、カード可、6席、2015年3月31日開店。口コミ(2022年9月〜2026年5月): 常連の多い隠れ家、江戸前の鮨、赤うに、路地の奥に看板だけ、経験30年の主人、刺身の盛り合わせ、赤貝・中トロ・鯛、蟹・のどぐろ・鰹のたたき、大将が選ぶ日本酒、最高のこはだ、締めの潮汁、ホタルイカ、ソフトシェルクラブ、白魚、焼き蛤、鯛のあら炊き、トロとたくあん、小鯵、穏やかな主人、おまかせに好みを追加、鮨懐石、飲み物は高め、コースは割安、予約が取りにくい、蟹、ふぐの白子。

cultural_comfort.note: Six-seat counter with regulars; reservations needed.

osaka_misono_hozenji.gf_detail: Not gluten-free in practice: kara-age, simmered and sauced dishes.
osaka_misono_hozenji.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 17:00–22:30 (L.O. 22:00); closed Sunday (Tabelog). Reserve: fills within minutes (December 2025). Cards accepted; no e-money or QR (Tabelog).
osaka_misono_hozenji.notes: [Japanese · a chicken specialist beside Hōzenji] A chicken restaurant in the building next to Mizukake Fudō, cooking domestically raised young chickens from sashimi to rice. The assorted chicken sashimi is fresh and bouncy, the thigh tataki hits hard with garlic, and the kara-age, especially the crisp wings, is a favorite; one diner ordered four plates of grilled cartilage. Look also for fried chicken skin rolled with green onion, liver, gizzards and a spicy simmered chicken skin to eat over rice. Courses run to mizutaki, refined in chicken flavor, with rice porridge, and there is a dry curry omurice. Service is quiet but kind, with plates split for groups. Seats fill within minutes, so reserve. Sake is limited; beer and shochu are there.

chef_bio.background: Chicken specialist using domestically raised young chickens; official site tori-misono.com (Tabelog).

anecdotes.text: "The sashimi was fresh and had a nice bounce. The kara-age was juicy with a strong meaty flavor… The tataki was robust with a great garlic kick." — October 2025.
"We started with chicken breast and wings, followed by a delicious mizutaki (chicken hot pot). The refined flavor of the chicken in the mizutaki was outstanding." — March 2026, course.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式 tori-misono.com。食べログ(店舗会員): みその、大阪市中央区難波1-2-10 法善寺MEOUTOビル1F、法善寺水掛不動尊の隣のビル、月〜土17:00〜22:30(L.O.22:00)、日曜休み、カード可、電子マネー・QR不可、国産の若鶏を使った鶏料理の専門店。口コミ(2025年2月〜2026年3月): 誕生日にコース、刺身・手羽先・ドライカレー、カウンターと座敷、なんこつ唐揚げ、鶏刺し、手羽先唐揚げ、レバー焼き、ドライカレーオムライス、サラダ、レバー煮、鶏皮、チゲ、日本酒の種類は少なめ、焼酎、奥の個室のテーブル、刺身は新鮮で弾力、ジューシーな唐揚げ、にんにくの効いたたたき、ねぎを巻いた鶏皮揚げ、取り分けてくれる、ピリ辛の鶏皮煮とご飯、焼きなんこつ4皿、予約なしで入れたがすぐ満席、刺身の盛り合わせ、砂肝、口数は少ないが親切、コースの水炊きと雑炊。

osaka_yakitori_jin_souemoncho.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 18:00–3:00 am; closed Sunday (Tabelog). Six counter seats; call ahead (2016 review). Cash only: no cards or e-money (Tabelog). Smoking allowed (Tabelog).
osaka_yakitori_jin_souemoncho.notes: [Yakitori · a six-seat back-alley counter in Souemoncho] A tiny yakitori counter so deep in a Souemoncho back alley that one diner would never have found it unaided. The current owner took over in January 2014 and kept the name. Skewers are generous and thick: bonjiri, skin, negima, tsukune and yagen nankotsu are favorites. The house draw for some is the chicken liver sashimi, cooked at low temperature. Also on the board: thigh tataki, gizzard, red sausage, a spicy yam kimchi, smashed cucumber, and a chazuke in chicken broth to finish. It's a proper old-school local joint. One diner waited a while for orders. Only six seats, so call ahead. Open until 3 am; closed Sundays. Cash only.

chef_bio.origin: Current owner took over 11 January 2014, keeping the name (Tabelog)

anecdotes.text: "When I think of Jin, I can't help but crave… liver sashimi! It's cooked at a low temperature, and the texture is so amazing that I always want more!" — September 2023.
"The interior is cozy, with about five counter seats, making it easy to connect with the chef." — October 2026.

osaka_isshin_hozenji.hours_raw: Tue–Sun 17:00–22:00; closed Monday (Tabelog). Cards accepted; no e-money or QR (Tabelog).
osaka_isshin_hozenji.notes: [Sushi · a ten-seat counter by Hōzenji's Mizukake Fudō] A long-established sushi counter in the Hōzenji lanes, close to Mizukake Fudō, with ten seats and the calm air of a long-established shop. The head chef is particular about fish, and once turned away a red clam that wasn't fresh enough. Blue crab is a long-running highlight. A July 2026 dinner ran from sashimi and rock oysters to uzaku, an abalone gunkan and tekka maki, with Kamo Tsuru Gold sake, which carries petal-shaped gold leaf. Stories of the shop's history come with the meal. It is pricey: reviewers spent ¥15,000–30,000, and one walk-in felt the bill outran the value. Closed Mondays.

anecdotes.text: "I actually wanted to order my favorite red clam, but it was deemed not fresh enough upon opening, so I couldn't have it… This time, the standout ingredient was the blue crab." — February 2024.
"We also enjoyed a unique Japanese sake, Kamo Tsuru Gold, which features cherry blossom petal-shaped pure gold leaf." — July 2026.

osaka_yakiniku_p_takanosuke.gf_detail: Not gluten-free in practice: marinated meats and yukhoe sauce; miso with the senmai.
osaka_yakiniku_p_takanosuke.hours_raw: Daily 18:00–2:00 am; closing days may vary (Tabelog); one diner noted 3 am (February 2025). Cash only: no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog). Smoking allowed (Tabelog).
osaka_yakiniku_p_takanosuke.notes: [Yakiniku · a six-seat alley counter where the master grills] A hidden yakiniku counter in a narrow Souemoncho alley, next door to Hiromiya. There are no grills at the seats: the master grills each cut and serves it at its best, so up to about seven diners squeeze in close. Portions are about half the usual size, so you can try many cuts. Start with white senmai, when there is any, with sesame oil, salt and a moreish miso. Then go to aburi yukke, wagyu tataki, salted tongue, outside skirt and kalbi. A Korean-style cold tofu with kimchi and seaweed is a side. It's easy to drop by alone, and the owner suits the room. Open late, to 2 am. Cash only; smoking allowed.

chef_bio.background: Counter yakiniku; the owner grills for guests (2022–2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The master cooks and serves the meat, so there are no grills on the tables… Each serving is smaller than average, at about half the size of portions in other restaurants, allowing you to try a variety of dishes." — September 2024.
"Both the yukke and tataki were incredibly fresh and delicious! What's more, the owner grills the meat for you!" — August 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ(店舗会員): 焼肉P貴之助、大阪市中央区宗右衛門町6-25、なんば駅から徒歩5分、毎日18:00〜翌2:00、休みは変わることも、カード・電子マネー・QR不可、カウンター6席、20人まで貸切可、喫煙可。口コミ(2022年12月〜2026年8月): 細い路地の隠れ家、一人でも入りやすい、ユッケとハラミ、焼き加減がちょうどいい、見た目より味の多彩なメニュー、白センマイは数が少ない、朝3時まで、カウンターのみ、マスターが焼いてくれる、韓国風冷奴、センマイ刺しにごま油と塩、味噌、塩タン、ほほ、ミノ、旧清流会館とホテルの隣の路地、ヒロミヤの隣、7人ほどで満席、量は半分ほどで品数を楽しめる、炙りユッケ、和牛たたき、和牛カルビ。

osaka_ikareta_noodle_fish_tons.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–15:00 (L.O. 14:55) and 18:00–22:00 (L.O. 21:55); Saturday morning ramen 7:00–9:00; open through to the New Year break, check social media (Tabelog). One bowl per person; no eating while looking at phones (Tabelog). Cards, e-money and QR accepted (Tabelog).
osaka_ikareta_noodle_fish_tons.notes: [Ramen · Shinmachi's Ramen 100 seafood-tonkotsu tsukemen] A tsukemen shop near Nishi-Ohashi, open since 2017 and picked for Tabelog's Ramen OSAKA 100 in 2023, 2024 and 2025. The dipping sauce is thick pork bone and seafood, bonito-forward, and it clings to homemade thick, flat noodles chilled in water for a chewy, wheaty bite. Add diced onion and aji daikon as you go, then finish with soup or Dive Rice, a small bowl of rice with green onion to drop into the sauce. The TOKYO-X premium tsukemen (¥1,500) carries juicy rare chashu. There's also a seafood tonkotsu ramen (¥1,000) with a free large size. On Saturdays there is a 7 am morning ramen, such as a charcoal-grilled chashu miso. Noodles were too soft for one pair. Expect a short line at lunch. House rules: one bowl each, no phones while eating.

chef_bio.background: Tsukemen shop (Tabelog, staff-maintained); Tabelog Ramen OSAKA 100 2023, 2024 and 2025.

anecdotes.text: "The broth is a rich seafood and pork bone base, thick and hearty, with a strong flavor of both seafood and pork. The noodles are homemade, flat, and thick." — October 2026, ajitama tsukemen.
"The broth is a double soup made from chicken and pork bones, lightly emulsified with ginger and kombu kelp… The chashu is charcoal-grilled and hung to dry." — October 2026, Saturday morning ramen.

osaka_seimenya_nipponbashi.hours_raw: Mon and Wed–Fri 11:00–15:00; Sat–Sun 11:00–16:00; closed Tuesday; hours may change (Tabelog). Ticket machine (August–October 2026). PayPay accepted; no cards or e-money (Tabelog). Families and wheelchair users welcome (Tabelog).
osaka_seimenya_nipponbashi.notes: [Ramen · a two-person tsukemen shop at the south end of Otaroad] A 13-seat noodle shop at the southern tip of Nipponbashi's Otaroad, open since 2013 and run by two: a chef in the kitchen and one person serving, both notably polite. The draw is chicken-shoyu tsukemen (¥1,330 for medium): smooth, glossy noodles and a gentle soy dipping sauce full of chicken, with tenkasu and black shichimi, mild enough to drink on its own. There's also chicken paitan on medium-thick curly noodles; this autumn it carried a curry ball you break into the broth. In summer the chilled niboshi soba (¥1,250) comes with a rice to drown in the cold broth. One bowl took about 15 minutes. Lunch only; closed Tuesdays.

chef_bio.background: Two-person tsukemen and ramen shop on Otaroad (2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The soy sauce-based dipping sauce was not too strong and incredibly delicious!… I personally prefer a gentler flavor that I could drink on its own." — October 2026, chicken-shoyu tsukemen.
"I was advised to pour the broth over the rice, giving it a chilled chazuke-like experience. The furikake sprinkled on the rice added a nice accent." — August 2026, chilled niboshi soba.

osaka_kawachiriba_minamisenba.hours_raw: Lunch only: Mon–Sat and days before/after holidays 11:00–14:30; closed Sundays and holidays (Tabelog). Cash only: no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog).
osaka_kawachiriba_minamisenba.notes: [Ramen · clam-broth chuka soba for lunch near Nagahoribashi] An eight-seat lunch counter near Nagahoribashi, open since 2021, built on a clear shellfish broth. The kaidashi shio ramen tastes most clearly of clam, light yet deep. The asari shoyu is lighter still, too subtle for some, and the shichimi from Sakai's Yamatsu Tsujita lifts it. Smooth, chewy noodles are the constant praise; one diner ordered extra noodles. Thin chashu, seasoned egg and menma complete the bowl, and the shio set adds rice with clam tsukudani; sansho on the counter suits it. There's also a meat soba, and it once served cold pasta. A calm room with many women dining. Lunch only, Monday to Saturday. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Clam-broth chuka soba, lunch only (Tabelog, staff-maintained).

anecdotes.text: "The broth was a beautifully clear clam soup, and the noodles were smooth and delicious!… The clam tsukudani (sweet simmered clams) was also great with both the rice and ramen." — September 2026, shio set.
"You can really taste the clam broth in this shio ramen. The richness is sufficient even without changing the flavor of the soup." — June 2026.

osaka_gyukotsu_ou_minamisenba.notes: [Ramen · a one-person beef-bone counter near Nagahoribashi] A nine-seat counter open since 2016, run single-handed by the owner, serving beef-bone ramen until midnight. The broth is rich yet clean, with no off-flavor, and one diner called it richer than tonkotsu. The recommended shio bowl and the white broth come over thin straight noodles that one diner likened to Hong Kong wonton noodles, topped with tender beef tendon or stew-soft chashu, fragrant fried garlic chips, sesame and pickled ginger. Extra noodles are free, or rice at lunch. Summer brought a chilled bowl with pork shabu-shabu, aosa and lemon. Service is warmer than the name suggests: one diner was seen off at the door. Buy a ticket at the machine; PayPay accepted.

chef_bio.background: Beef-bone ramen counter run by the owner alone (May 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "The broth was free of any unpleasant odors or bitterness, and it was very delicious! It had a nice thickness and was easy to drink!" — October 2026.
"The fragrant fried garlic chips are the standout feature of this restaurant, adding an incredible aroma that makes you want to eat more." — May 2026, shio beef-bone ramen.

osaka_aoba_ramen_honmamonya.notes: [Ramen · kakuni and bok choy shoyu ramen by Matsuyamachi] A ten-seat counter 100 m from Matsuyamachi Station, run single-handed by a polite owner, with a spotless room. The Aoba ramen (¥1,700) is the reason to come. A light soy broth of chicken feet and vegetables with Japanese dashi carries medium-thin straight noodles. On top sit two slabs of sweet, meltingly tender kakuni, plus bok choy, a hard-boiled egg and a whole stick of menma. Skip the kakuni for ¥1,100, or go to five slices for ¥2,700. A newer pork-trotter soba with scallion oil (¥1,000) brings three trotters on the side. House condiments let you layer the flavor. It opens at noon, late for ramen. Cards and cashless accepted.

"The braised pork—it's delicious! It's tender and packed with flavor… The light broth allows the deliciousness of the pork to stand out even more." — August 2026.

osaka_kitakata_bannai_namba_nipponbashi.notes: [Ramen · Kitakata-style chashu ramen between Nipponbashi and Ebisucho] A branch of the Bannai chain, open since 2023 and one of the few places in Kansai for Kitakata ramen. The bowl is a light, clear pork broth seasoned with soy, over flat, chewy, high-hydration curly noodles. Melt-in-the-mouth chashu and thick-cut green onion top it. The roast pork ramen was ¥1,360 in September 2026. From 1 September the Mega Chashu ramen piles on about 24 slices, nearly double. There's also a miso ramen that won over one shoyu loyalist, a limited chicken shio with yuzu, and a mini aburi yakiniku don. Friendly staff; it was quiet at 22:00 one Friday. Buy a ticket at the machine. Open until 22:00.

chef_bio.background: Branch of the Kitakata Ramen Bannai chain; official site ban-nai.com.

anecdotes.text: "The pork clear soup is incredibly delicious. The noodles are perfectly chewy and smooth. The chashu is unmatched in flavor." — September 2026, roast pork ramen ¥1,360.
"The flat, high-hydration curly noodles pair well with the light soy sauce broth." — September 2026, Mega Chashu ramen.

osaka_menya_gaten_z_otaroad.notes: [Ramen · Jiro-style mazesoba on Otaroad] A Jiro-style mazesoba counter on Otaroad, open since 2017; one regular also goes to the Namba branch. The MAZE soba comes with 300 g of thick, smooth noodles and tender chashu, and noodles, vegetables, garlic and fat can be adjusted for free. Garlic hits hard, so go light before a meeting. The Taiwanese version (¥1,150) adds ground meat, chives, nori, fish powder and egg yolk; there's a mildly hot curry mazesoba and a brothless shio ramen with yuzu that one fan rates the best of its kind. The counter is stocked with black pepper, shichimi, Sichuan pepper, chili oil and vinegar, kimchi is free, and a ¥100 gacha picks a surprise topping like mentaiko. Allow ten minutes. Cash-only ticket machine.

chef_bio.background: Mazesoba shop on Otaroad (Tabelog, staff-maintained); a Namba branch also operates (May 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "The noodles were soft, wide, and flat, topped with ground meat, chives, seaweed, fish powder, garlic, green onions, and an egg yolk, giving it a Jiro-style twist." — February 2026, Taiwanese MAZE soba ¥1,150.
"The 100 yen gacha topping added a playful element, and I was lucky enough to get mentaiko, which paired wonderfully with the rich mazesoba." — May 2026, shoyu mazesoba.

osaka_mugen_ramen_nambanaka3.notes: [Ramen · Mugen's beef-bone shop in Nambanaka 3-chome] A Mugen Ramen shop open since 2020 near Daikokucho, whose beef-bone aroma greets you at the door. The beef-bone white soup ramen is rich and creamy, topped with tender roast beef and fatty brisket. The spicy chashu noodles (¥1,350) add Sichuan pepper, garlic chives and heat a little milder than Shin Ramyun. Opinions split: one diner found it phenomenal, one found the chashu tough and over-seasoned, another didn't think it worth the price, and the mini chashu rice bowl was mushy and salty for one diner. Staff and customers are mostly from overseas, and service was slow for one diner. Open until 23:00. See also Mugen Ramen Sennichimae and Shinsaibashi.

anecdotes.text: "It had a rich, creamy texture with a deep, flavorful essence. The toppings included tender slices of beef roast and fatty brisket." — April 2026.
"The Sichuan pepper on top really adds a great touch! The broth is delicious. The spiciness is a bit milder than Shin Ramyeon." — June 2026, spicy chashu noodles.

osaka_yakitori_mumei_no_name.notes: [Yakitori · a seven-seat Tajima-chicken counter in Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A dark, grown-up yakitori counter on the fourth floor of a Higashi-Shinsaibashi building, open since 2024 behind an understated sign. Tajima chicken is grilled over charcoal in front of you with refined, light seasoning. The ¥9,000 omakase runs eight skewers, three appetizers and a finish. It opens on seared thigh with fresh pepper, then breast, crunchy gizzard, salt-crisped skin, heart in a sweet tare, tsukune with a rich egg, a boned wing with zucchini, and negima. In between come a liver pâté that won over one liver skeptic, a chicken-broth chawanmushi and homemade pickles. Finish with yakitori don, grilled rice-ball soup or soboro don. À la carte works too. Reserve; closed Wednesdays.

chef_bio.background: Charcoal yakitori counter using Tajima chicken (January 2026 review; Tabelog, staff-maintained).

anecdotes.text: "The yakitori is made with Tajima chicken, and the smoky aroma from the charcoal is prominent… The seasoning is refined and not overly strong, making it a perfect match for drinks." — January 2026.
"The appetizer 'Liver Pâté' was surprisingly good. I usually dislike liver, but this had no off-putting smell and was quite tasty." — August 2026, ¥9,000 omakase.

osaka_sakana_shimada.notes: [Japanese · a seasonal fish counter in Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A small, calm Japanese restaurant on a third floor in Higashi-Shinsaibashi, built around seasonal fish. The chef came from Asai, a well-known Osaka restaurant, and one diner felt a similar vibe. Order à la carte or book an omakase from ¥10,000 ahead. Sashimi might be kensaki squid, tuna, hamo and Wakayama octopus. A January visit brought soy-grilled cod milt, fried oysters and a salmon kasujiru; an August one, abalone, a fragrant dobin mushi and a miso-grilled fish to close. The small dishes are built for sake. The counter is intimate: with no other guests, one diner felt the chef was listening in. Guests are seen to the elevator. Reviewers spent about ¥10,000–30,000.

chef_bio.background: Chef previously worked at Asai, a well-known Osaka restaurant (June 2026 review). Seasonal fish counter (Tabelog, staff-maintained).

anecdotes.text: "The abalone was tender, the dobin mushi (teapot steamed dish) was fragrant, and the sashimi tuna was exquisite… The grilled fish at the end had a soft texture with a rich miso flavor." — August 2026.
"We started with fresh oysters, and I was surprised by their impressive size, followed by a luxurious assortment of sashimi." — May 2026, omakase.

osaka_nihonshuya_ichiro.gf_detail: Not gluten-free in practice: tempura and soy-simmered dishes.
osaka_nihonshuya_ichiro.vegan_detail: Not vegan: offal, sardines and chashu among the snacks. Pumpkin tempura has been on the menu (March 2026); ask about the batter and frying oil.
osaka_nihonshuya_ichiro.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 19:00–2:00 am; Sat–Sun 14:00–24:00; closes irregularly; hours may change (Tabelog). Holidays open from 14:00 (September 2026). QR accepted; no cards or e-money (Tabelog). Smoking allowed (Tabelog).
osaka_nihonshuya_ichiro.notes: [Bar · a sake bar behind an unmarked third-floor door] A sake bar on the third floor of the White Building, open since 2015 behind a door that shows nothing of the inside, a little daunting at first. Inside are a counter, a table and a warm welcome. Sake pours by the masu, about a full 180 ml for ¥800–1,000, from labels such as Ishizuchi, Utsukushihime and a limited Kujiranami. The snacks stand out: simmered Saga beef offal that won over a tripe skeptic, tamahimo-ni, simmered sardines, chashu, and tempura of firefly squid or pumpkin. Weekdays bring regulars, weekends overseas visitors, and the TV shows baseball or racing. Weekends and holidays it opens at 2 pm for daytime drinking. Smoking allowed.

chef_bio.background: Sake bar; regulars on weekdays, overseas visitors on weekends, per the owner (December 2025 review).

anecdotes.text: "The simmered offal is absolutely fantastic! It seems to be made with Saga beef offal… Especially the honeycomb tripe, which is one type of offal I usually dislike, but this completely changed my perception." — October 2025.
"With prices under JPY 1000 for 180ml of sake, the cost performance is excellent!" — September 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: にほん酒や一路、大阪市中央区東心斎橋2-7-12 ホワイトビル302、月〜金19:00〜翌2:00、土日14:00〜24:00、不定休、QR可、カード・電子マネー不可、10席(満席時は立ち飲み)、喫煙可、2015年11月27日開店。口コミ(2025年10月〜2026年10月): ホワイトビル3階、畳屋町と笠屋町の間、入口にカウンター・奥にテーブル、野球中継、ハートランドの瓶ビール、日本酒いろいろ、ホタルイカとかぼちゃの天ぷら、日本酒の日、玉ひも煮、チャーシュー、Kujiranamiの限定酒、Sagaの牛ホルモンの煮込み、ハチノス、祝日の15時に先客4人、競馬中継、Ishizuchi、いわしの煮付けとUtsukushihime、常連と外国人客、平日は常連・週末は外国人が多いと店主、日本酒は800〜1,000円、枡で一合ほど、ウイスキーも、土日祝は14時開店、ドアが中の見えない作りで入りにくい、温かく迎えてくれる、コスパがいい、品揃えが素晴らしい。

cultural_comfort.note: Overseas visitors common on weekends (December 2025); no English evidence found.

osaka_steak_house_juju.gf_detail: Not gluten-free in practice: garlic soy sauce and ponzu with the steak.
osaka_steak_house_juju.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a steak and seafood teppan counter.
osaka_steak_house_juju.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 17:00–22:30 (L.O. 21:30); closed Sunday (Tabelog). 10% service charge at dinner (Tabelog). Courses tailored to budget and occasion on request (Tabelog). Cards accepted; no e-money or QR (Tabelog).
osaka_steak_house_juju.notes: [Steak · a quiet teppan counter on Dotonbori's west end] A basement teppanyaki counter just west of Midosuji, open since 2009, quieter than its Dotonbori address suggests and used for celebrations. Behind a heavy door, a veteran chef grills at the 11-seat counter and chats as the courses unfold. Expect a salad with two homemade dressings, grilled vegetables and tofu, live kuruma ebi from the tank (head and legs crisped for the wine), sazae, with abalone in the tank too, and a grilled Hokkaido caciocavallo. The main is Kagoshima tenderloin, with paper-thin garlic crisped in butter, homemade garlic soy and ponzu; one diner prefers it to the fattier ribeye. Reviewers spent about ¥8,000–15,000. A 10% service charge applies. Closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Teppanyaki counter; the chef grills and talks with guests (2023–2025 reviews); official site steak-jyu-jyu.com.

anecdotes.text: "The steak was served with thinly sliced garlic grilled with a generous amount of butter and low heat… It was served with homemade garlic soy sauce, ponzu, and coarsely ground black pepper." — March 2023, Kagoshima chateaubriand.
"The ribeye has a good amount of fat, but I recommend the tenderloin." — April 2025.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式 steak-jyu-jyu.com。食べログ(店舗会員): すてーきはうす寿々、大阪市中央区道頓堀2-1-7 サン道頓堀ビル B1F、なんば駅25番出口から徒歩3分、月〜土17:00〜22:30(L.O.21:30)、日曜休み、ディナーはサービス料10%、カード可、電子マネー・QR不可、鉄板カウンター11席、2009年3月3日開店、予算や目的に合わせたコース、誕生日や記念日、接待にも。口コミ(2022年11月〜2026年9月): 御堂筋の西側で静か、お祝いに、地下の重い扉、12席ほどの鉄板カウンター、車海老のコース13,000円、90年代の洋楽、自家製ドレッシング2種のサラダ、ベテランの料理人、エリンギ・豆腐・菜の花・れんこん、水槽の九州産天然の車海老、頭や脚はパリパリに、サザエ、黒鮑、Hokkaidoのカチョカヴァロ、Kagoshimaのシャトーブリアン、バターで焼いた薄切りのにんにく、自家製のにんにく醤油、ポン酢、リブロースより赤身がおすすめ、落ち着いた雰囲気、特別な日に。

osaka_sushi_kiwami_higashishinsaibashi.gf_detail: Not gluten-free in practice: soy sauce, tempura and a sukiyaki-style pot in the course.
osaka_sushi_kiwami_higashishinsaibashi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a sushi kaiseki course.
osaka_sushi_kiwami_higashishinsaibashi.hours_raw: Daily 18:00–23:00; closes irregularly, see Instagram (Tabelog). 10% service charge (Tabelog). Reserve by phone (Tabelog). Cards accepted; no e-money or QR (Tabelog).
osaka_sushi_kiwami_higashishinsaibashi.notes: [Sushi · a sushi kaiseki counter in Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A modern sushi counter at the back of a building's ground floor, open since 2021 behind a noren, with amber light on the counter and private tables with sliding doors. The ¥22,000 omakase runs 15 to 18 items, mixing Edomae sushi with kaiseki dishes. It opens with fig tempura and ginger. Then come kombu-cured flounder and botan shrimp, shima-aji, a fragrant seared scallop roll with sudachi, and Hokkaido uni served in a glass. Kinmedai, nodoguro, toro and marinated akami follow, with seasonal tempura and a sukiyaki-style pot where cotton candy melts in. It closes with a toro-taku roll and a wasanbon pudding. A 10% service charge applies. Hard to find; reserve by phone.

chef_bio.background: Sushi kaiseki counter (Tabelog, staff-maintained); official site susi-kiwami.com.

anecdotes.text: "The sukiyaki-style hot pot was served with cotton candy to dissolve, adding a fun visual element to the experience." — September 2026, omakase.
"The course offered not only sushi but also a variety of Japanese dishes, culminating in a homemade wasanbon pudding for dessert." — September 2026, ¥22,000 omakase.
